content.text: Zhou Pingfan, take a look at Xingren. Something seems off lately. I took a photo—it keeps licking the same spot, and the fur there has already thinned out. Its energy level isn’t great either. Last time we talked about pet care details, you even asked about feeding methods. Now, facing this situation, it’s really worrying.

Got the photos. It does look a bit unusual. Could it be due to the change of seasons? Or has there been any recent stressful events? I remember you mentioned last time that the temperature at home has been stable, so it probably isn't an issue with environmental temperature changes.

It shouldn't be due to the change of seasons; the temperature at my home has been consistently stable. Perhaps it's because I've been too busy with work lately, working overtime frequently, and spending less time with it, which might be causing it some anxiety? I was in pretty good shape when we last met for a meal, but I didn't expect the project to become so urgent recently.

Well, cats can easily develop behavioral issues due to changes in their environment or neglect from their owners. Are you still using the automatic feeder you mentioned earlier? Has there been any change in their diet?

The feeder has been working normally. Here is the recent diet list I’m sending you for review, and it should be fine. Compared to the feeding plan I shared last time we discussed pet care, it remains largely consistent.
The list has been received, and the types and portions of food seem quite reasonable, similar to what you shared before. However, excessive licking might not just be a dietary issue.
Yeah, I'm worried too. Last time we talked about the details of pet care, you even asked about feeding methods. Now, encountering this situation is really anxiety-inducing.

Don't worry too much; let's analyze this rationally. Since your diet isn't an issue, it might be a skin problem or a psychological factor. I think it's better to see a doctor—it’ll save you time and effort. Just like when we discussed work issues last time, leaving professional matters to professionals is the most efficient approach.

I agree, but I’ve been extremely busy with work lately, as my client’s project is on a tight deadline, and I can’t find the time to take him. Could I ask you to help take Almond for a check-up? Last time we met for a meal, you chose a Sichuan restaurant with great value for money, and now you’re helping out again—you’re truly considerate and reliable.
No problem, my recent projects aren't too tight, so I can help. Just let me know the hospital address and any precautions, and I'll arrange a time to take it there.
Thank you so much! This is the address of the animal hospital. I often go there, and both the environment and service are great. I'll send you the map.
Address received, it looks like it's not far from me. Are there any precautions I should take when taking Almond out? For example, regarding how to carry her or any calming techniques.

It's best to use a carrier when going out, with a familiar blanket inside. Speak softly to comfort it on the way and avoid sudden noises. Oh, and it likes having its chin scratched, which can help it relax.
Okay, noted. I'm free on Saturday morning and can come to pick it up, which gives us more time. Is that convenient for you?

I'm available on Saturday morning. Thank you, Zhou Pingfan. Last time we made plans, you chose a Sichuan restaurant with great value for money, and now you're being so helpful again. You're truly considerate and reliable.
You're welcome. It's only natural for friends to help each other out. I'll contact the hospital in advance to make an appointment and ensure the process is efficient.
Great, I feel much more at ease with your help. I'll leave the almond to you, and please let me know as soon as the test results come out.
Don't worry, I will provide timely feedback. Even though you're busy with work, make sure to take breaks and don't get too anxious—problems can always be resolved.
Well, thank you for your comfort. Once this is over, let's plan a meal together—my treat, as a way of saying thanks.
Alright, it's settled then. See you on Saturday, and let's keep in touch.
